newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah little changed in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah little changed in dull trade.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was steady against the dollar in dull late trading on Thursday, with the central bank raising its fixing as anticipated, dealers said.

"It was a sleepy afternoon. Bank Indonesia depreciated the rupiah by one point as expected," one major local bank dealer said. The central bank raised its intervention band to 2,328/2,520 and the conversion rate to 2,328/2,376.
The dealer said a rise of tom/next swaps in the morning was brief. It later eased back to 1.30/1.35 points after reaching a high of 1.6/1.8 at the opening.
But longer-term swaps remained little changed after driving up earlier on rises in tom/next swaps.
One-month swap was at 15.75/16.75, two at 33.5/34.5, three at 49.50/50.00 and six at 97.0/98.0 points.
The local bank dealer said the rises need not be due to anticipation of tight liquidity on Friday but could be because of some temporary mismatches.
He said some foreign operators wanted to square positions but hit the market at the wrong time.
"The market was thin and already squared," he said, adding that the market had stabilised after the brief rise.

Dealers said offshore operators were seen sustaining selling interest in the dollar, possibly due to inflows to subscribe to the public float of Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) shares. BNI's public offering of almost 1.1 billion shares will be from November 4 to 7. The listing will be on November 25.

The local bank dealer said there could be some worries of tight liquidity because of the float, but he expected stable conditions because the money would be kept with underwriters for some time. There could be tightness later, because BNI is likely to park the money in central bank papers (SBIs), he said.
